chunks: From him, from Saʿd ibn Ismāʿīl, from his father Ismāʿīl ibn ʿĪsā, who said:

I asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام about a female servant belonging to a man’s child, or to his father, or to his family: is it lawful for him to uncover himself in front of her, or not? He said: “As for the child, I do not see any harm in it.”

key_terms.الْخَادِمِ: the female servant being asked about in the ruling
key_terms.بَيْنَ يَدَيْهَا: in her presence or before her
key_terms.فَلَا أَرَى بِهِ بَأْسًا: I do not consider there to be any harm in it
key_terms.لِأَهْلِهِ: belonging to his family or household
key_terms.يَتَجَرَّدَ: to uncover himself or remove his clothing

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a man to uncover himself before a female servant belonging to his child or family?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal question posed to Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام regarding the permissibility of a man uncovering himself before a female servant connected to close family members. The Imam عليه السلام specifically states that in the case of the child’s servant, he does not regard it as problematic, indicating a jurisprudential ruling tied to familial ownership and domestic relations.
